doc.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Pay for the fraternity gigs
summary: About twelve dollars a gig, fifty or sixty for a weekend, and occasional twenty dollar tips from alumni.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: That’s a great description of your weekend. How much money would you have netted for that kind of work?

Usually for each of those gigs you’d get about twelve dollars so as you could see I mean you might, I mean those were big weekends. Most times you’d just go out there’d be a Saturday night row. But you know you could make fifty, sixty dollars. And every once in a while there’d be a very wealthy alum there who loved Dixieland that would come up and give everybody in the band a twenty dollar bill.
That’s a big event, isn’t it. That’s great.
